chunks.subject: AP Computer Science A
chunks.title: Q2 — Class (9 points)
chunks.content: AP CS A FRQ 2 (Class Design), 9 points, per-point criteria then penalties (max 3/question). Task: write class SignedText with instance data, a constructor, getSignature(), and addSignature(String). Pt1 correct class header (public class SignedText, no parentheses/params, not private). Pt2 declares appropriate PRIVATE instance variable(s) and the constructor initializes them from the parameters (not static, not declared inside the constructor, must use both params). Pt3 correct constructor header SignedText(String, String) (not private/static). Pt4 correct method headers: public String getSignature(), public String addSignature(String) (correct names, return, and parameter types). Pt5 compares the first name to the empty string (explicitly or via length). Pt6 determines the correct signature string in both cases (first initial + '-' + last, or just last) — the getSignature algorithm point. Pt7 uses String methods with correct syntax throughout and calls at least one element-accessing method (substring/indexOf/charAt), not only length/equals. Pt8 identifies the three addSignature cases (no-match, match-start, match-end) with appropriate conditions. Pt9 addSignature returns the correct String in all three cases — the algorithm point. Common failure: omitting private (Pt2); a class header with parentheses/params like a record (Pt1); substring index errors in the match-start case (Pt9); a method header missing its return type (Pt4).

chunks.subject: AP Computer Science A
chunks.title: Q2 exemplar — Sample 2A, 7/9
chunks.content: Q2 scored 7/9. Earned Pt1, Pt2, Pt3 (miscased 'signedText' constructor not penalized), Pt5, Pt6, Pt7, Pt8. Lost Pt4 (the addSignature header was missing its String return type) and Pt9 (match-start case used text.substring(len-sig, len), returning part of the parameter plus the signature instead of the correct string). Missing () on a getSignature call was not penalized. Illustrates a strong class marred by a header return-type omission and a substring-index error.

chunks.subject: AP Computer Science A
chunks.title: Q2 exemplar — Sample 2B, 6/9
chunks.content: Q2 scored 6/9. Earned Pt1, Pt4, Pt5, Pt6, Pt7, Pt8. Lost Pt2 (instance variables declared without private), Pt3 (constructor parameters declared without their String types), and Pt9 (match-start case called signature.substring(s+1), going one character too far). Illustrates the frequent 'forgot private' and off-by-one substring errors.

chunks.subject: AP Computer Science A
chunks.title: Q2 exemplar — Sample 2C, 3/9
chunks.content: Q2 scored 3/9. Earned Pt4 (both method headers), Pt5 (empty-string check via length), and Pt7 (String syntax). Lost Pt1 (class header written with parentheses and parameters, record-like but no record keyword), Pt2 (no private instance variables), Pt3 (no constructor header), Pt6 (firstName.substring(0) returns the whole string, not the first letter), Pt8 (match-end condition subtracted 1 incorrectly; = vs == not penalized), and Pt9 (called getSignature with arguments and appended a signature to a signature). Illustrates that a record-style header with no fields collapses the structural points.
